q: How well do the Kundrat/PARTRAC analytical formulas agree with an independent MCTS code (Geant4-DNA or TRAX-CHEM) run on the same PARTRAC target geometry (10 um spherical lymphocyte nucleus, 6.6 Gbp, G0/G1) for the same ion/energy grid, across the full published LET range and specifically at the SSB dip (5-20 keV/um) and DSB peak (100-500 keV/um)?
basis: The paper validates the formulas only against its own PARTRAC MCTS outputs. Refs 28-31 note ongoing Geant4-DNA implementations of comparable physics, but no cross-code residuals are published. Refs 12-14 (Friedland group PARTRAC benchmarking) show that PARTRAC-vs-Geant4-DNA yield differences at matched geometry can reach a factor of 2 in DSB cluster fractions. No such cross-code validation of these formulas exists in the current literature (Section 4, Discussion, para 3).
next_steps: Run Geant4-DNA (available on uicgpu) with the 'dna' physics list on a spherical water target with implanted geometric-DNA scoring at 6.6 Gbp equivalent for at least protons (0.5-100 MeV/u, 6 energies) and He-4 (1-100 MeV/u, 6 energies); score SB/SSB/DSB per Gy per Gbp; compute residual (formula - MC)/formula at each LET; report chi^2 per damage class. This is exactly the multi-week study the current paper does not perform.

q: Are the formulas safe to extrapolate outside their 0.25-512 MeV/u training range, in particular for ultra-low LET (electrons and photon secondaries, LET << 0.3 keV/um) and ultra-high LET (very slow heavy ions near/past the Bragg peak, LET > 1000 keV/um for O-16/Ne-20)?
basis: Eq. (2) contains a logistic overkill turnover (denominator (p4*LET)^p5) that is monotone-suppressing above ~500 keV/um; the fit does not have a physical stopping-power ceiling built in. The paper explicitly declares the fit range and says nothing about extrapolation safety (Section 2.2, last paragraph). For SB (Eq. 1), the low-LET plateau p1 is hand-fixed across ions; whether this survives at LET below the fit floor is untested.
next_steps: (a) Evaluate the formulas at LET = 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 keV/um and inspect whether SB/SSB drop unphysically below the low-energy electron-track regime (they should tend to the electron/gamma limit, ~130 SB/Gy/Gbp per PARTRAC 2003 refs). (b) Evaluate at LET = 2000, 5000 keV/um and inspect whether DSB drops through zero or asymptotes to an unphysical negative value (Eq. 2 numerator is positive, denominator positive, so it asymptotes to LET^(p3-p5) which for typical p3~1.5, p5~1.2 goes as LET^0.3 -> keeps growing slowly; likely wrong physically). (c) Publish a documented 'safe range' addendum.

q: Can the analytical fits be re-parameterized to carry a chromatin-configuration variable (condensation fraction, heterochromatin/euchromatin ratio, S-phase replication-fork density) so they apply beyond the PARTRAC G0/G1 spherical-lymphocyte target?
basis: The paper's target model is a single G0/G1 lymphocyte-nucleus configuration. All 540 fit parameters absorb the chromatin state implicitly. Damage yields for mitotic chromatin (~5x more compact) or S-phase (replication forks, altered DSB chemistry) are known experimentally to differ by up to 2-3x. The formulas as-published cannot be dialed to cell state (Section 2, Model section).
next_steps: Run PARTRAC (or Geant4-DNA-Chem, which we can) with 3 target geometries (G0/G1 spherical, condensed mitotic, S-phase with replication-fork nodes) at 3 ion/energy points each. Fit an added exponential-envelope factor exp(-alpha * chromatin_density) to (p1, p2, p4) in Eq. (1) and to numerator/denominator scales in Eq. (2). If a single 3-parameter chromatin correction absorbs the geometry variation to <20%, publish it as an extension formula.

q: How do the DSB / DSB-cluster / DSB-site yields from Eq. (2) translate into cellular survival predictions when fed into an established biophysical survival model (LEM-IV, MKM, RMF, or PARTRAC's own repair chain), and does the analytical shortcut give the same survival curves as a full MCTS+repair chain would?
basis: The paper stops at DSB-yield output; downstream survival is out of scope. But the raison d'etre of these formulas is treatment planning, where survival - not DSB yield - is the endpoint. Whether the DSB->survival step is dominated by DSB total, DSB clusters, or DSB sites (each of which has its own overkill-turnover shape) is not addressed. LEM-IV in particular is sensitive to DSB cluster fraction, so the shape of Fig. 4 matters more than Fig. 3 for RBE prediction.
next_steps: Wire the analytical yields into LEM-IV (public C++ implementation) and MKM (public Python implementations exist) as the DSB-input layer; compute survival curves S(D) for 2 Gy fractions across the 9 ions at 4 LET points each; compare against experimental survival data compiled in PIDE database (public); report RBE_10% residuals. Free endpoints only (LEM-IV + MKM are CPU codes).

q: Are the direct-vs-indirect damage split assumptions (linear SB probability 0->1 from 5-37.5 eV; 65% breakage per OH attack) robust, and how sensitive are the analytical formulas to reasonable alternative assumptions used by other track-structure groups (KURBUC uses different indirect chemistry; Geant4-DNA-Chem has energy-dependent OH yields)?
basis: The paper commits to fixed direct/indirect probabilities inherited from earlier PARTRAC papers (Friedland refs 14-16). But e.g. KURBUC uses stochastic indirect chemistry with time-resolved OH scavenging; Geant4-DNA-Chem in 2020+ versions has energy-dependent radiolytic yields. If direct/indirect split changes, the shape of the Lorentzian dip in Eq. (1) (which is driven by the indirect channel at intermediate LET) will change. This sensitivity is not analyzed anywhere in the paper.
next_steps: Re-fit Eq. (1) parameters (p2, p3, p4, p5 for the SSB indirect channel) under two alternative indirect-chemistry assumptions: (a) OH breakage probability scaled by 0.75x and 1.25x uniformly; (b) OH breakage probability with energy-dependent scaling matching Geant4-DNA-Chem 11.2 yields. Report parameter shift magnitude and yield residual at LET = 1, 10, 50, 200 keV/um. If parameter shifts are <20% for the plateau and <2x for the dip depth, the formulas are robust; if not, publish the sensitivity band as a systematic on the fits.
